Narrative: A 3'UTR variant in mut-16 might alter expression of a factor required for small RNA-mediated chromatin regulation and transgene/germline silencing; such chromatin misregulation can indirectly change transcriptional programs that specify neuronal fates, but direct evidence linking MUT-16 to AMso asymmetric divisions is lacking [Effect=3_prime_UTR_variant; impact_bucket=MODIFIER; QUAL=31.4; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="mut-16 is required for RNAi, transgene silencing and low transposon mobilization; predicted to influence chromatin organization."]
rationale: MUT-16 is required for small-RNA-mediated silencing and chromatin regulation; a 3'UTR variant could alter its expression and thereby indirectly perturb fate-determining transcriptional programs in AMso daughters.

WB_Overview: Enriched in neurons based on RNA-seq studies. Is affected by csr-1 and rrf-2 based on RNA-seq and microarray studies. Is affected by tryptophan; resveratrol; and allantoin based on microarray studies. Is predicted to encode a protein with the following domains: Receptor L-domain superfamily; Receptor L domain; Receptor L-domain; and SPS2 domain-containing protein.
Narrative: Missense in neuron-enriched irld-66 (receptor L-domain family) could alter signaling in amphid-associated cells; given AMso are amphid socket glia and irld family members are neuron-expressed, altered ligand/receptor interactions could conceivably influence AMso division outcome though mechanism is unclear [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=39.3; WB_Overview="Enriched in neurons; predicted receptor L-domain protein."]
rationale: IRLD-66 is neuron-enriched and encodes a receptor-L family protein; a missense could perturb receptor-mediated signaling that indirectly alters AMso division outcomes.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable RNA binding activity and zinc ion binding activity. Involved in mRNA stabilization and positive regulation of meiotic nuclear division. Located in cytoplasm. Expressed in several structures, including Psub3; Psub4; Z2; Z3; and germ line.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: nos-3 encodes a homolog of Drosophila NANOS that physically interacts with FBF-1 (similar, though not orthologous, to Drosophila PUMILIO); NOS-3 is required in development of the hermaphrodite germ-line to promote the switch from sperm to oocyte production, perhaps by forming a complex with FBF-1 that controls fem-3 mRNA.

rationale: NOS-3 is a Nanos homolog with primary germline function but alters post-transcriptional regulation; a missense could have systemic developmental effects that indirectly influence AMso fate decisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable ribosomal protein S6 kinase activity. Predicted to be involved in TORC1 signaling. Predicted to be located in cytoplasm and nucleoplasm. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Coffin-Lowry syndrome; alcohol-related birth defects; and non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability 19. Is an ortholog of several human genes including RPS6KA1 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A1); RPS6KA2 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A2); and RPS6KA3 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A3).
rationale: RSKN-1 is predicted to act in TORC1 signaling as an S6 kinase homolog and has possible chromatin-related user annotations; a missense might alter growth or chromatin signaling but direct evidence for AMso fate impact is limited.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable amidophosphoribosyltransferase activity. Predicted to be involved in purine nucleotide biosynthetic process. Expressed in intestine. Is an ortholog of human PPAT (phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate amidotransferase).
rationale: PPAT-1 is a metabolic enzyme in purine biosynthesis; while metabolic deficits can produce pleiotropic developmental defects, there is no specific link to asymmetric neuronal fate choice, making it a low-probability candidate for MCM loss.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable calmodulin binding activity and syntaxin-1 binding activity. Involved in regulation of multicellular organismal process; spermatogenesis; and synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Located in presynaptic active zone. Expressed in head neurons; neurons; tail neurons; and ventral nerve cord. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Is an ortholog of human UNC13A (unc-13 homolog A); UNC13B (unc-13 homolog B); and UNC13C (unc-13 homolog C).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: unc-13 encodes at least five protein isoforms that regulate neurotransmitter release by altering the conformation of syntaxin; UNC-13 proteins are required for normal pharyngeal pumping and thrashing in liquid, normally short lifespan, normally large brood sizes, and full adult body sizes; UNC-13 proteins have orthologs in vertebrates and Drosophila; UNC-13 proteins are complex, with multiple C2, phorbol ester-binding, and DUF1041 domains; UNC-13 protein form is localized to most or all synapses; many of the unc-13 mutant alleles with viable phenotypes are transcript-specific, while homozygotes with an unc-13 null (deletion) allele die as paralyzed first-stage larvae.

WB_Overview: Involved in several processes, including response to anesthetic; response to ethanol; and response to toluene. Located in axon. Expressed in head neurons; nerve ring; nervous system; tail neurons; and ventral cord neurons. Used to study alcohol use disorder. Is an ortholog of human UNC79 (unc-79 homolog, NALCN channel complex subunit).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: unc-79 encodes a novel, conserved protein; unc-79 functions in a pathway with unc-77 and nca-2, which encode alpha-1 subunits of voltage-insensitive cation leak channels, to regulate locomotion and the response to specific volatile anesthetics; unc-79 exerts its effects on these processes, at least in part, by regulating the levels of UNC-77 and NCA-2 proteins; an unc-79::gfp reporter is expressed in the nervous system in ventral nerve cord neurons in L2 and L3 larvae and in one or two head neurons in adults; UNC-79 exhibits a punctate staining pattern in ventral nerve cord and nerve ring processes, and this staining is dependent upon UNC-80, UNC-77, and NCA-2.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable transmembrane transporter activity. Predicted to be involved in chloride transmembrane transport and sulfate transmembrane transport. Predicted to be located in plasma membrane. Expressed in body wall musculature; excretory cell; hypodermis; intestine; and neurons.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: sulp-1 encodes one of eight C. elegans members of the sulfate permease family of anion transporters; by homology, SULP-1 is predicted to function as an anion transporter that regulates cellular pH and volume via transmembrane movement of electrolytes and fluids; a sulp-1::GFP transcriptional fusion is expressed strongly in several neurons, weakly in hypodermal cells and the intestine, and very faintly in the excretory cell and body wall muscle.
Narrative: Missense in sulp-1 (sulfate permease) is expressed in some neurons; altered ionic transport could affect neuronal health but does not provide a specific mechanistic explanation for conversion of AMso asymmetric divisions to symmetric glial divisions, so it is a weak candidate for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=8.9; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="sulp-1 encodes a sulfate permease family member expressed in neurons and hypodermis."]
rationale: SULP-1 is a sulfate permease expressed in some neurons and hypodermis; a missense could affect ionic homeostasis and neuronal health but lacks a specific mechanism for converting AMso asymmetric divisions to symmetric glial outcomes.
